Why the price ladder beats static chips

  • Spatial information for free. Eye sees instantly if NOW is below stop, inside entry zone, extended past entry, near T1, or beyond T2. Static STOP $241 · T1 $260 chips force mental math.
  • Entry-quality signal built-in. NOW marker position relative to the green entry segment instantly flags FRESH / PULLBACK / EXTENDED / MISSED. No separate entry-quality tag needed.
  • Risk-reward visible as proportional width. Red segment (stop distance) vs green→blue (upside to T2) — eye reads the asymmetry without computing 1:1.3 or 1:3.0 ratios.
  • Trade phase encoded in color. Red = stop-out zone · green = entry zone · amber = in-trade running zone · blue = T2-zone or beyond. Same color story across every ticker.
  • Sample 1 (DELL): NOW just inside entry · cleanest setup · color story green-to-amber-to-blue with NOW pegged to entry zone.
  • Sample 2 (NVDA): NOW past entry into the amber zone · extended · the visual itself screams "wait for pullback".
  • Sample 3 (AMD): NOW between stop and entry · ladder shows trade still valid · entry is +1.8% above current.
UI architect note
The ladder replaces 6+ static chips with a single visual that carries more information. This is the difference between reading a number and perceiving a relationship. For a trading app where every second of attention matters, the ladder wins.
